raw_segments.text: The ghost replied, Your piety has paid all needful rights
To rest my wandering shade, But cruel fate and my more cruel wife
To Grecian's swords betrayed my sleeping life.
These are the monuments of Helen's love, The shame I bear below, the marks I bore above.
You know in what deluding joys we passed the night that was by heave and decreed our last.
For when the fatal horse, descending down, pregnant with arms,
Orwhelmed th, unhappy town she feigned nocturnal orgies,
Left my bed, and mixed with Trojan dames, The dances led then, waving high her torch,
The signal made, which roused the Grecians from their ambiscade.
With watching overworn, with cares oppressed, Unhappy I had laid me down to rest,
And heavy sleep my weary limbs possessed.
Meantime my worthy wife our arms mislaid, And from beneath my head my sword conveyed,
The door unlatched, and with repeated calls Invites her former lord within my walls.
Thus in her crime her confidence she placked, And with new treasons would redeem the past.
What need I more?
Into the room they ran, And meanly murdered a defenseless man.
Ulysses, basily born, first led the way, Avenging powers, with justice if I pray,
That fortune be their own another day.
But answer you, and in your turn relate, What brought you living to the Stygian state,
Driven by the winds and errors of the sea, Or did you heave in superior duma bay,
Or tell what other chance conducts your way, To view with mortal eyes our dark retreats,
Two molts and torments of th, infernal seats.
